title: Impact triangle commitments + 1:1 prep — Leah Park
notes:
Purpose: short, tactical prep to use in 1:1 with manager. Focus: what I deliver next 6–12 weeks, evidence stories, and three explicit asks. Keep this lean — can paste into Slack 1:1 thread as agenda.

Top-line one-liner
- Reduce new-hire ramp time for infra/dev tooling by 40% over next 6 months by shipping onboarding playbook + automation for account provisioning.

Impact triangle (why / how / what)
- Why: Growth of Dedicated customers is bottlenecked by our ability to spin isolated environments quickly. Onboarding friction is a recurring support cost and customer NPS drag.
- How: Standardize the onboarding checklist, automate the 70% of setup steps we repeat, add a "first-week runbook" and triage play for escalations. Coordinate with infra platform and solutions eng.
- What (concrete output): onboarding playbook (doc + runbook), 2 automation scripts (account provision + baseline infra), and a training session for SEs + CS. Measured by mean time-to-first-successful-inference (MTF-SI) and checklist completion rate.

Metrics I own / want to track (baseline + target)
- MTF-SI baseline: 12 days -> target: <=7 days (6 months)
- Checklist completion (manual) baseline: 38% -> target: >=85% (3 months)
- Escalation volume from CS baseline: 1.8/week -> target: <0.6/week (3 months)

Evidence bank (short stories I can tell)
- June onboarding for X customer: took 18 days, major delay caused by manual KMS onboarding and missing firewall step; I stepped into cross-team chat, added checklist item, but no automation.
- Internal pilot (Oct): scripted 3 steps and cut one onboarding from 14 -> 8 days (single data point). Use as proof-of-concept but call out scale risk.

Risks & mitigations to raise early
- Risk: infra team capacity constrained this quarter. Mitigation: scope for minimal viable automation first (priority 1: KMS + network), request a shared part-time engineer from infra or prioritize under Dedicated backlog.
- Risk: compliance/legal edge cases slow automation. Mitigation: draft a compliance-friendly playbook first, iterate with security for guardrails.

Manager asks (explicit) — rank-ordered, quick to action
1) Headcount/time: 0.2 FTE infra engineer for 10 weeks (or a scoped sprint). Rationale: automation yield is high; without this I can deliver playbook but not automation.
2) Prioritization: move onboarding automation to top of Dedicated backlog for Q2 sprint planning (flag for PM alignment).
3) Promotion calibration: add my 6–9 month impact plan as input for next calibration cycle; I want manager support to position for L4->L5 consideration in H2 (will share narrative + evidence).

Quick wins (next 6 weeks)
- Draft playbook skeleton and checklist (week 1–2)
- Run internal pilot with one solutions engineer (week 3)
- Ship first automation script for account provisioning (week 4–6)
- Training session + feedback loop with CS (week 6)

Signals for success (what I will update you with in 1:1)
- Completed checklist doc + sample filled checklist
- Automation PR merged + test logs demonstrating reduced steps
- Data: MTF-SI samples for 3 onboardings post-automation

Coaching asks (how you can help)
- Help me frame the promotion narrative: where do I need to be bolder in claims? Which stakeholder outcomes matter most to reviewers?
- Introductions: connect me with Maya (security) and Elena (product-dedicated PM) to unblock compliance and prioritization conversations.

Open questions I want to discuss
- Do you think 0.2 FTE is reasonable ask vs. asking a feature sprint dedicated to this (one-time)?
- If promotion slate requires cross-team endorsements, who should I prioritize for early alignment?
- Is there appetite to include this as a "customer success metric" owner role so the project gets backlog weight?

Personal operating constraints
- Deep work windows: Tue/Thu mornings only for heads-down (block time in calendar)
- Travel: on-site week of 2026-04-13 (limit actionables that week)
- Energy: capacity is 70% this quarter (managing two parallel projects) — want manager awareness in prioritization decisions.

Notes to self (write-up items for promotion packet)
- Bullet list of measurable wins (dates + metric deltas)
- Code & docs links (PRs + Confluence pages)
- Upward feedback from CS/SE customers (quotes)

Next 1:1 agenda (3 items, 20–30 mins):
1) Quick readout on pilot results + ask for 0.2 FTE approval (10 min)
2) Promotion narrative: 2–3 areas I want feedback on (10 min)
3) Blockers and next-week priorities (5–10 min)

Scratch items (to flesh into doc later)
- Template checklist: environment, KMS key, VPC rules, IAM roles, quota request steps, sample test inference script, contact matrix.
- One-pager for exec view: ROI estimate (time saved * weekly saves * seat-cost) and risk reduction.

Trailing todo (log) — short-hand
- [ ] Draft playbook skeleton
- [ ] Create pilot test runbook
- [ ] Draft PR for automation script
- [ ] Ask Noah for infra contacts
- [ ] Pull last 6 onboardings from CS notes
reflection: Feels productive — have one data point that proves value but need to scale. Want manager alignment on prioritization and a small engineering allocation. Keep this doc as living artifact; I will prune after each 1:1.
